root_cause.text: In `parse_dacl()`, the code reads `sid.sub_auth[2]` to recover mode bits after a matching SID comparison, but `compare_sids()` only compares the minimum number of subauthorities, so a server-supplied ACE with only 2 subauthorities (e.g., `{88, 3}`) can match the 3-subauthority `sid_unix_NFS_mode`, leading to an out-of-bounds read of `sub_auth[2]`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "A malicious server can return an ACE with num_subauth = 2 and sub_auth[] = {88, 3}, which still matches sid_unix_NFS_mode and then drives the sub_auth[2] read four bytes past the end of the ACE." The patch adds the check `ppace[i]->sid.num_subauth >= 3` before the `compare_sids()` call.
